attribution.note: Zitron's own assessment in his own post.

semantics.note: Leaving out 'fairly straightforward' does not change the testable core: the announced AI integrations do nothing not seen elsewhere.

contract.note: Reading this as a functional precedent, with demonstrations counting, is ordinary and not stretched either way. Support needs all substantive capabilities covered. Contradiction needs proof of one unprecedented capability.

evidence.note: Apple's announcement sets out which features are being compared. It says nothing about whether they were new.
GrammarlyGO, March 2023, offered contextual rewriting and composing before WWDC. This covers the writing tools only.
Samsung's January 2024 Galaxy AI already had AI photo editing. Partial precedent only.
Bard Extensions, September 2023, pulled personal data across Google apps. Partial precedent; it does not cover Apple's cross-app actions or on-screen awareness.
Meta's AI stickers, September 2023, came before Genmoji. Partial precedent.

reviews.rationale: Earlier products match several features: writing tools, photo editing, stickers, and personal-data retrieval. The packet itself admits the feature-by-feature comparison is incomplete for cross-app actions and on-screen context. No item shows a feature without precedent. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own aside in his post.

semantics.note: In context, 'the future' means AI, so the normalised version is faithful. The claim says failure outright.

contract.note: Reading this as Wall Street lacking meaningful confidence in Google's AI position is an ordinary reading of a categorical 'failed'.

evidence.note: Yahoo Finance, May 15, 2024: Goldman Sachs called Alphabet the premier AI innovator after I/O. A prominent institution accepting the pitch inside the period. The original note is reported, not obtained.
A February 2024 share drop amid the Gemini image-tool problems. An earlier setback; it does not isolate the cause or show rejection continuing through June.

reviews.rationale: The claim says outright that Google failed to convince Wall Street. Weeks before the post, Goldman Sachs publicly called Alphabet the premier AI innovator. That is meaningful acceptance by a prominent institution and does not fit categorical failure. The February setback is earlier and does not show rejection continuing. The evidence is not a survey of investors.

attribution.note: The free-access and nothing-in-return assertion is Zitron's own. The Google/Anthropic talks are relayed from Gardizy's reporting, and the leverage clause is hedged with 'likely'.

semantics.note: Keeps 'effectively', the attribution to The Information, and the 'likely' hedge. The leverage part is speculative and is not scored.

contract.note: Reading 'nothing in return' as no direct payment is fair, since the passage itself talks about upselling. 'Hundreds of millions' is read as the potential audience. Both are ordinary in context.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement confirms free access without an account. It is a company disclosure.
Bloomberg, June 13, 2024: Apple is not paying OpenAI, with exposure to hundreds of millions of devices.
Federighi publicly named Gemini as a future integration on June 10, 2024. Shows pursuit, not a signed deal.
Engadget reported talks with Anthropic within the period. It does not verify Gardizy's report.
Notes distribution benefits and possible conversions to paid plans. This matters only under a broader 'no benefit' reading, which the contract does not use.

reviews.rationale: Free integrated access, no direct payment from Apple, a potential reach of hundreds of millions of devices, and Apple pursuing Google and Anthropic are all documented within the period. The leverage clause is hedged and not scored. The Gardizy attribution itself was not verified, but other contemporaneous reporting corroborates what it describes.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, but built on a premise he calls speculation.

semantics.note: The antecedent and the speculative service-agreement premise are both kept. The consequent depends on 'I'd speculate... likely requires', so the claim is hedged at its root.

contract.note: The contract rightly requires both an adoption shortfall and reserved capacity. Because the premise is hedged speculation, the claim should not be scored either way.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own court filing shows it cut its adoption forecast by January 2025, which partly bears on the antecedent. It says nothing about reserved capacity or idle resources. A party's self-description.

reviews.rationale: The resources in question exist only under a service agreement Zitron says he speculates Apple 'likely' requires. That is hedged language and is not scored. Separately, the reserved-capacity antecedent is unknown: no evidence shows such capacity or whether it sat idle. Only the adoption shortfall is partly documented.
